terms.comment: Literally “don’t knock over the wagon”. We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

evidence: Plaut. Ep. 4.2.22: Periī, plaustrum perculī! (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Plautus’s proverb is a cry of one who has ruined himself, not a warning to others.
terms.gloss: I’ve upset the cart, I’m done for

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
